narrative.overview:
Source Tree feels like opening a well-kept repository: a quiet README pane, a directory drawn with thin rules, and real project names where you expect to find them. The repository metaphor helps people find the work; it doesn't imitate an editor or a terminal.

A bold name and plain reading copy keep the profile personal. Monospace picks out paths and identifiers. Flat spruce-black surfaces leave mint for links, small icons, and keyboard focus; a separate tint shows where a fragment link landed.
keyCharacteristics: Spruce-black ground, softly separated surfaces, and mint for actions.
Chivo headings, system-sans reading copy, and monospace paths.
Square, ruled rows with native links and persistent fragment states.

rules.name: The Mint Signal Rule
rules.body: Use the brightest color for things people can follow or need to locate. Keep paragraphs neutral; use the stronger tinted panel and its own keyline to show where a local jump landed.

rules.name: The Paths Are Not Paragraphs Rule
rules.body: Use monospace for identifiers, Chivo for page and section headings, and system sans for reading. The `.8125rem` and `.875rem` tiers are intentional annotation and compact text roles, not defaults for long-form reading or substitutes for link target size.

rules.name: The Flat Workspace Rule
rules.body: No shadows. Separate regions with tone, space, or a one-pixel keyline. Show interaction with a fill, underline, or outline rather than lift.

dos: Do use native anchors and meaningful fragment targets so navigation and content work without JavaScript.
Do preserve the skip link, heading hierarchy, visible link labels, and distinct keyboard-focus outlines.
Do keep decorative branch, folder, and arrow SVGs out of the accessibility tree.
donts: Don't add shadows, round the structural frames, or turn repository rows into detached cards.
Don't add fake controls or terminal chrome. Use inline vector marks alongside text rather than raster decoration or glyphs standing in for icons.
